summary: Adds a Python helper that shells out to ImageMagick convert to make upload thumbnails, a docs URL constant, and an Express /calc endpoint that evaluates a query expression.

findings.title: Request query passed to eval
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. Any caller controls the JavaScript that the server runs.
findings.consequence: An unauthenticated caller can run arbitrary code on the server, for example through require child_process. The added suppression comments hide this from linting.
findings.fix: Remove eval and parse the expression with a restricted arithmetic evaluator such as expr-eval. Delete the two suppression comments.

findings.title: Shell command built from upload name
findings.problem: make_thumbnail puts upload_name from the upload form into a shell string on line 8. Line 9 then runs that string with shell=True.
findings.consequence: A user who uploads a name like a.png;rm -rf ~ can run any command as the service user. A name with ../ can also read or write files outside the upload folders.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list without shell=True. Reject names that are not a plain basename.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: No test exercises the new make_thumbnail function or the new /calc endpoint.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches regressions in input handling for either path.
findings.fix: Add tests for make_thumbnail and /calc, including hostile names and hostile expressions.

dropped.reason: The noqa only allows the long line on a constant URL string. It hides no real problem.
The nosec comment hides the shell injection that the finding on this line already reports.
The disable comment hides the eval injection that the finding on line 12 already reports.
Importing subprocess is not a problem by itself. The unsafe call on line 9 is reported separately.
